texts.preamble: Hanumantharaju vs Sridevi B. Math on 28 February, 2025 Kabc020306752021 Before The Motor Accident Claims Tribunal Court of Small Causes, Bengaluru. Dated This The 28th Day Of February 2025 Present: Sri.Kumara.S (B.A., Ll.B) Vii Addl. Scj and Acjm, Member, Mact-3, Bengaluru. M.V.C.No.5210/2021 Petitioner : Sri.Hanumantharaju, S/o Garudaiah,
texts.facts: This petition is filed by the petitioner U/Sec 166 of M.V. Act 1989 against respondents for seeking compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by him, in the Motor Vehicle Accident. 02. The brief facts of case of the petitioner is that:- That on 24-10-2021 at about 07.30 p.m, when the petitioner was riding two-wheeler/Suzuki Access bearing No.KA-02-HT-1268 along with his wife Mamatha as pillion rider, proceeding from (SCCH-3) 3 M.V.C.No.5210/2021 Mallappanahalli to Bengaluru, on NH-75 i.e., Kunigal- Nelamangala Road, they came in front of Mahadevapura Petrol Bunk, Nelamangala Taluk, at that time the driver of Car bearing No.KA-41-MD-2550 proceeding front to the petitioner was suddenly, reckless and negligently stopped the car in front of the petitioner's two-wheeler and consequent to which the petitioner's two-wheeler hit to the hind portion of the car and accident was occurred. Due to terrific impact the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries and was immediately shifted to VP Magnus hospital, Nelamangala, wherein after first aid he was shifted to Citi hospital, Bengaluru and admitted as inpatient and has spent huge amount towards medical expenses, conveyance, nourishment and attendant charges and prior to accident the petitioner was hale and healthy and was aged about 43 years and was working as employee in Kaviraj Cooker Factory, Luggere, Peenya, Bengaluru and drawing salary of Rs.18,000/- p.m. Due to accidental injuries the petitioner is uanble to attend his duty and hence sustained loss of income. The accident is occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending Car involved in the accident and in this regard the Nelamangala Traffic Police have registered a case against driver of the said offending (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.5210/2021 Car. Hence, the respondent No.1 being the RC owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurer of the said offending Car, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- with interest and costs. 03. On service of notice, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared before the tribunal through their counsels, but only the respondent No.2 has filed written statement. 04. The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied the entire case of the petitioner and further denied alleged accident, negligence of the driver of offending Car, age, avocation, income of the petitioner and nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and treatment taken by the petitioner and expenses incurred by the petitioner and admits that this respondent has issued the policy in respect of the Car bearing No.KA-41-MD-2550, but the original copy of the policy is in the Hanumantharaju vs Sridevi B. Math on 28 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98360407/ 2 possession and control of the respondent No.1 and the liability of this respondent is limited to the terms and conditions of the policy and contended that the driver of the said Car has no valid and effective driving licence and the owner allowed the driver to drove the same knowingfully well that he has no valid and effective driving licence and thereby there (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.5210/2021 is clear violation of policy terms and conditions. There is no negligence on the part of the driver of offending Car and petitioner being a rider of two-wheeler rode the same without wearing safety headgear and it is violation of M.V. Act. The compensation claimed is highly exorbitant and pray for dismiss the petition with costs against respondent No.2. 05. 06. In order to prove his case, petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and got examined MRO as (SCCH-3) 6 M.V.C.No.5210/2021 PW.2 and through them got marked 20 documents as Ex.P.1 to 20 and closed his side evidence. The respondent No.2 got examined MRO as RW.1 and through him got marked 3 documents as Ex.R.1 to 3 and closed its side evidence. Further, MRO of Citi hospital, Bengaluru, is examined as PW.2 and he he has produced MLC register, Case sheet and X-ray as per Ex.P.18 to 20. Medical Expenses 2,42,893-00 Total 3,02,893-00 22. Accordingly I hold that, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.3,02,893/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
